newsitem.title: UK: Britons racist, but tolerant of immigrants - study.
newsitem.headline: Britons racist, but tolerant of immigrants - study.

text.p: Britons are much more tolerant of refugees than politicians imagine although racism remains widespread, a report published on Tuesday said.
The report by the left-leaning Institute for Public Policy Research (IPPR) also found many of Britain's ethnic minorities loathe each other.
Opinion polls in the study found 75 percent of whites believed refugees needed help and support and the same percentage thought a ban on immigration would do nothing to end racial prejudice.
Only one percent viewed immigration as a problem.
"Race and immigration is way down the list of concerns, well behind crime, law and order and unemployment," the IPPR said.
"However tempting, politicians would be unwise to play the race card at the next election," it added.

Britain's Conservative government, facing a general election by May, has taken a tough line on immigration and last year introduced an asylum bill under which hundreds of asylum-seekers have been jailed while they wait for their cases to be heard.
Those who were concerned about immigration did not make any distinction between the races of the immigrants, the IPPR said.
"We are just as worried about Australian dentists as we are about people coming from anywhere else," said Nick Moon of NOP, which conducted the opinion poll.

Moon said that because NOP believed that people would lie if simply asked whether they were racist, respondents' attitudes were gauged by asking indirect questions, such as whether they believed there was racism in Britain.
The poll found that 90 percent of white Britons thought there was some prejudice against minority groups.
"People won't readily admit to their prejudices, but by saying there was racism, these people were thereby admitting they are racist," Moon concluded.

The study found 91 percent of Afro-Caribbeans, 84 percent of Asians and 90 percent of Jews believed there was prejudice against minorities. But the only people who believed there was anti-semitism in Britain were Jewish people.

Some of the fiercest racism was between ethnic groups. Debra Mattinson, one of the researchers, quoted one Asian woman as saying that "most West Indians are undesirable" and a Jewish woman as saying Blacks should be "sent home."
The researchers said that since the study was the first of its kind in Britain, they were unable to say from their findings whether racism was on the rise or not.
